added_source.name: Overture Maps Foundation, buildings theme: features whose origin is not OpenStreetMap (footprints detected from imagery by machine learning)
added_source.licence: ODbL 1.0 (Overture: "License for theme: ODbL"); per origin dataset below
added_source.nature: Machine detections, not surveyed and not reviewed by a person. Not in OpenStreetMap at the date of our extract.

datasets.attribution: Google Open Buildings. Available under CC BY 4.0. Via Overture Maps Foundation.
Global ML Building Footprints. Licensed by Microsoft under the Open Database License. Via Overture Maps Foundation.

added_source.rule: OpenStreetMap is the base: every building of our own OSM extract is kept unchanged. An Overture building is added only if none of its sources is OpenStreetMap and (1) it does not overlap our OSM extract or an addition already accepted: dropped if its centroid is inside an OSM footprint, an OSM centroid is inside it, or the outlines intersect at all (outer rings); (2) it is plausible: at least 25 m2, confidence at least 0.7 where the source gives one, not above 5000 m2 unless its confidence is at least 0.8, and at least 4 m wide (short side of its smallest enclosing rectangle; containers, trailers and vehicles are narrower); (3) its centroid is on land inside a municipio; (4) it is not a small footprint (under 60 m2) whose outline comes within 1.5 m of an OSM footprint (taken as part of the mapped building). Tests run in that order and a candidate is counted under the first one it fails. Added records have bit 7 (0x80) of kind set; kind is house under 400 m2, otherwise other; height is the source's own or 0.

record: uint8 kind (low 7 bits; bit 7 = added: detected from imagery, not in OpenStreetMap)
int16 ground_dm (ground elevation at the centroid from the 1 m lidar DEM, decimetres above the datum in "ground"; -32768 = no lidar value)
int8 place_half_m (half metres to add to ground_dm to get the elevation of the 10 m terrain the scene is drawn on; used only to stand the building on that terrain)
encoding.uv: fx = lonToTileX(lon, 14) - x; fy = latToTileY(lat, 14) - y (0..1 across the tile: fx east, linear in longitude; fy south, linear in Web Mercator y). u = round((fx + 0.25) / 1.5 * 65535); v = round((fy + 0.25) / 1.5 * 65535). Decode: fx = u / 65535 * 1.5 - 0.25; fy = v / 65535 * 1.5 - 0.25.
encoding.ring: outer ring only, closing vertex not repeated, winding as in OSM (not normalised); rings above 64 vertices simplified (Douglas-Peucker)
encoding.assignment: a building is stored once, in the tile containing the centroid of its outer ring
encoding.added_flag: kind & 0x80: the footprint comes from added_source (a machine detection), not from OpenStreetMap; kind & 0x7f is the kind. In each tile the OpenStreetMap records come first, then the added ones.
encoding.ids: tiles/bld/14/{x}/{y}.ids beside each tile: one text line per record, in record order, "<gers>,<osm>,<height source>". gers: the Overture Maps GERS id (a stable feature id; for an OSM building the id of the Overture feature carrying it, for an addition its own), empty where there is none. osm: "w<id>" or "r<id>" for the OpenStreetMap way or relation, empty for an addition. height source: osm (height tag), lidar (measured from the 3DEP 2018 lidar point cloud, data/hazards/heights), levels (building:levels x 3.2 m + 1 m), parts (its tallest building:part), ovt (the detection source, via Overture), usas (FEMA USA Structures), empty (none: height_half_m is 0).

ground.source: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1 meter Digital Elevation Model, bare earth, from lidar
ground.statistic: median of the 1 m cells within 2 m of the centroid

datum.vertical: Puerto Rico Vertical Datum of 2002 (PRVD02), EPSG:6641
datum.how_confirmed: USGS WESM.csv (the 3DEP work-unit register) gives vert_crs for every work unit behind these tiles; the vendor DEM metadata gives altdatum/altunits. The GeoTIFFs themselves carry no vertical CRS and no unit tag, and their sidecar XML only carries the national boilerplate quoted below, which names NAVD88 (a datum that does not exist in Puerto Rico).
vendor_altdatum: Puerto Rico Vertical Datum of 2002, Geoid 12B
Virgin Islands Vertical Datum of 2009, Geoid 12B
datum.caveat: These projects also cover the U.S. Virgin Islands, whose part is referenced to the Virgin Islands Vertical Datum of 2009 (WESM vert_crs 6642 and/or vendor metadata; see virgin_islands_parts, which lists each such part with its bounding box and the number of Garita buildings inside it). No building lies inside any of those boxes, so every value here comes from a PRVD02 work unit.

heights_lidar.source: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) lidar point clouds, Entwine Point Tiles on AWS Open Data (usgs-lidar-public)
heights_lidar.flown: 2018-04 to 2019-04 (USGS project PR_PRVI 2018, after hurricane Maria)
heights_lidar.statistic: 90th percentile of the roof last returns minus the ground beside the building, or their median where the roof has two heights (the 90th percentile more than max(3 m, a quarter of the median) above the median: a tower over its podium, a tree over a house); data/hazards/heights/meta.json, method
heights_lidar.rule: taken for every building with a measured value, except where OpenStreetMap carries its own height tag (ids: osm); the ids file says lidar where it was taken
